title: M1: prove a MinHook detour survives Arxan's integrity checks
description:
THE GATE FOR EVERY FEATURE. DS2 SOTFS carries 48 Arxan stubs and 286 Arxan-redirected functions. er-hook is MinHook -- it patches prologues in .text, which is what an integrity check looks for. Until a detour is shown to survive, no plan that involves hooking is known to be viable.

HOOK SITE, derived statically (see docs/ARXAN-FOOTPRINT.md): RVA 0x00832e70. 2052 static call sites, prologue '48 89 5c 24 08' (one 5-byte instruction -- the trivial MinHook relocation case), 0x47 bytes long, NOT one of the 286 Arxan-redirected functions. Backup: RVA 0x008389e0, same prologue shape, 1287 calls.

DO NOT hook RVA 0x00832cb0 (12401 calls) or 0x00c2c9e0 (4866 calls). They are the two hottest functions in the game and BOTH are already Arxan-redirected -- they start with e9 rel32 into .text#2. Patching over Arxan's own jump would fail for reasons unrelated to the question.

Resolve the address as module_base + RVA at runtime. DllCharacteristics is 0x8160, DYNAMIC_BASE is set.
design:
The experiment must validate its own integrity, because a hit counter alone cannot distinguish 'Arxan reverted our patch' from 'the function was never called'. Four requirements:

1. HIT COUNTER logged periodically from inside the detour -- proves it fires.
2. BYTE-INTEGRITY POLLER: a thread that re-reads the bytes at the hook site every second, compares against what MinHook actually wrote, and logs any divergence WITH the observed bytes. This is what distinguishes reversion from non-invocation, and it works even if the function is never called.
3. TRAMPOLINE-INTEGRITY POLLER: same check over the trampoline. Arxan could corrupt the trampoline without touching the hook site, and the hit counter would go silent with the site looking pristine.
4. A/B ARM: an env var that SKIPS neuter_arxan. Without it, 'the detour survived' does not tell us whether Arxan was ever a threat or whether dearxan is load-bearing. Both arms must be run and both logged.

Also log process uptime and a heartbeat so a crash is distinguishable from a clean exit.
acceptance_criteria: Both arms run. With dearxan: detour fires, hook-site and trampoline bytes unchanged over 5+ minutes of play, process alive. Without dearxan: whatever happens is recorded with evidence -- reverted bytes captured verbatim, or a crash, or survival. The result is a stated fact either way, not an absence of failure.

title: Port scripts/ghidra/ from er-mods-rs -- the actual RE workhorse
description:
er-mods-rs/scripts/ghidra/ holds the static-analysis tooling that repo actually runs on: a large set of analysis scripts (BytePatternScan.java, CallSitesTo.java, CallArgConst.java, AnalyzeWithProgress.java and many more), plus bootstrap.sh and build-ghidramcp.sh for a Ghidra MCP daemon.

This is the higher-value port ahead of Frida, because DS2 is unusually amenable to static work: 5271 MSVC RTTI type descriptors and 587 DLRF-registered runtime classes mean class identification is reading names rather than inferring vtable shape. See docs/DS2-ENGINE.md.

Target artifact is darksoulsii-deobf.bin -- flat mapped image, file offset == RVA, VA = offset + 0x140000000. Confirmed to match the live process: DarkSoulsII.exe loads at its preferred base 0x140000000 under Proton despite DYNAMIC_BASE being set, so Ghidra addresses are live addresses 1:1.

First consumers: the Fe* menu work (M2-M5 of the quit-menu feature) and any DS2 bindings crate.

title: Create the DoltHub repo chozandrias/ds2-mods-rs so bd dolt push works
description: `bd dolt push` fails: 'push to origin/main: Error 1105: failed to get remote db; the remote: origin https://doltremoteapi.dolthub.com/chozandrias/ds2-mods-rs could not be accessed ... PermissionDenied'. .beads/config.yaml sync.remote is a DoltHub URL for user chozandrias, and either that database does not exist or the local credential cannot write it. The documented architecture in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md is refs/dolt/data on the git remote (Banon-Labs/ds2-mods-rs), which needs no DoltHub account. Until this is fixed every agent's issue state stays local-only: closes, creates and claims from parallel worktrees never reach anyone else. Either point sync.remote at the git remote or provision the DoltHub credential.
notes:
DIAGNOSIS CORRECTED (orchestrator, verified): the premise that beads syncs via refs/dolt/data on the git remote is NOT what this bd version does. Checked the working reference repo directly -- in ~/projects/er-mods-rs both 'git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*' and 'git for-each-ref refs/dolt/*' return EMPTY. er-mods-rs syncs to DoltHub (https://doltremoteapi.dolthub.com/chozandrias/er-effects-rs), not to a git ref. The CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md 'refs/dolt/data on your git remote' line is stale documentation, not the mechanism.

So the config here is right in form and the remote URL is the correct shape. The actual blocker is narrower: the DoltHub repo chozandrias/ds2-mods-rs does not exist. A dolt credential IS present (~/.dolt/creds/7ff2jv8jqsv152lcrs09jsqja079ipvuncsu5okmiv0lu.jwk) and works for er-effects-rs, so this is not an auth failure -- it is a missing repo.

FIX: create 'ds2-mods-rs' under the chozandrias account at dolthub.com, then 'bd dolt push' succeeds. Requires a browser login; no CLI path was found and the dolt binary is not on PATH (beads bundles its own). Until then issue state is local-only, though .beads/issues.jsonl IS committed and pushed to GitHub, so the issue LIST is not lost -- only the Dolt history is.
close_reason: DoltHub repo chozandrias/ds2-mods-rs created by the user; 'bd dolt push' now reports 'Push complete.' The intervening failure was a local internet outage (DNS lookup timeout on doltremoteapi.dolthub.com), not a permissions or config problem. Note for the record: the original issue premise -- that beads syncs via refs/dolt/data on the git remote -- is stale documentation. Verified against the working reference repo: in ~/projects/er-mods-rs both 'git ls-remote origin refs/dolt/*' and 'git for-each-ref refs/dolt/*' return empty. Beads syncs to DoltHub.

title: Tier 0: ds2-hook -- port er-hook (MinHook union) verbatim
description: crates/er-hook is 954 lines, ZERO dependencies. Shared MinHook FFI wrapper (MH_* externs, MH_STATUS, MhHook) plus the cross-DLL hook union (register_union_hook + chaining) and a pluggable log sink installed via set_hook_logger. Nothing in it is Elden Ring specific -- the only ER reference is a comment noting that the er_effects_union_register C export deliberately stays in er-quickload. Straight copy + rename.

title: Tier 0: ds2-game-base -- port the generic half of er-game-base, replace rva.rs
description:
crates/er-game-base is 2728 lines and splits cleanly by portability:

PORTS AS-IS (generic Win32/process utility, no game knowledge):
  mem.rs (490)  fault-safe RAM readers
  log.rs (264)  parameterized append-only file logger
  fnv1a.rs (82) fingerprints
  http.rs (339) one blocking WinHTTP GET

DOES NOT PORT (ER 1.16.2 specific -- drop or rewrite):
  rva.rs (283)             ER singleton RVA table, image base 0x140000000. REPLACED by a DS2 table built from the Ghidra work.
  filecap.rs (305)         FD4FileCap / DLString<wchar_t> / DLIO virtual roots -- FD4 does not exist in DS2 (2014).
  pgd.rs, profile_summary.rs, build_id.rs   ER save/profile layouts.

Note er-game-base's tier split (tier A zero-dep, tier B 'game-types' feature re-exporting eldenring + fromsoftware-shared) is the right shape to keep: the DS2 equivalent keeps tier A and leaves tier B empty until a darksouls2 bindings crate exists.

title: Tier 0: neuter Arxan via dearxan before installing any hook
description:
DS2 SOTFS carries 48 Arxan stubs. Measured with ~/projects/dearxan (examples/stub-audit): total_stubs=48, analyzed_ok=48, analyze_error=0, ok_with_encrypted_regs=5, ok_without_regs=43, total_region_lists=2969.

No code is actually encrypted -- apply_relocs_and_resolve_conflicts eliminated all 2969 candidate lists (survival test is 'decrypted entropy < current image entropy'), and the deobfuscate run applied 0 regions / 0 bytes. The candidates were varint false positives. But the 48 stubs are still real anti-debug/integrity code, and er-hook is MinHook -- it patches prologues in .text, which is exactly what an integrity check catches.

dearxan lists Dark Souls II SOTFS as a tested target and also handles the SteamStub 3.1 wrapper to recover the real entry point. Call its disabler from DllMain BEFORE any hook registration. Note the disabler feature needs windows-sys, so it only builds for the Windows target -- fine for the DLL, excluded from host-side crates.
acceptance_criteria: A trivial MinHook detour on a hot DS2 function survives >5 minutes of play without being reverted, crashing, or tripping an integrity check.

title: Tier 0: DS2 loader shell -- dinput8.dll proxy under Proton
description:
me3 cannot load DS2 (verified: --game accepts only darksouls3/sekiro/eldenring/armoredcore6/nightreign), so the ER [[natives]] path is unavailable. Use a DLL proxy on one of DarkSoulsII.exe's own imports.

Import surface (from its PE import table): WINMM.dll (5 thunks), steam_api64.dll (16), WS2_32.dll (43), fmodex64.dll (47), fmod_event64.dll (48), KERNEL32.dll (156), USER32.dll (61), ADVAPI32.dll (6), SHELL32.dll (2), dxgi.dll (1), ole32.dll (8), OLEAUT32.dll (3), d3d11.dll (1), DINPUT8.dll (1), XINPUT1_3.dll (2).

DINPUT8.dll is the smallest correct proxy surface: one forwarded export (DirectInput8Create), plus DllCanUnloadNow/DllGetClassObject/DllRegisterServer/DllUnregisterServer for correctness. Under Proton the native override must be set (WINEDLLOVERRIDES='dinput8=n,b') or Wine's builtin wins.
acceptance_criteria: Game boots under Proton with the proxy DLL in the Game/ dir; DLL writes a line to its own log file on disk; DirectInput still works (controller/keyboard input unaffected).

title: EPIC: port er-mods-rs functionality to DS2 SOTFS, one crate at a time
description:
Source: ~/projects/er-mods-rs (57 crates, Elden Ring, cross-compiled x86_64-pc-windows-msvc via cargo-xwin, loaded through me3 [[natives]]). Target: DARK SOULS II Scholar of the First Sin, appid 335300, buildid 9527516, /home/banon/.local/share/Steam/steamapps/common/Dark Souls II Scholar of the First Sin/Game/DarkSoulsII.exe, run under Proton Experimental 11.0-100.

Three verified blockers shape the whole port:
1. me3 does NOT support DS2. 'me3 profile create --game' accepts only darksouls3, sekiro, eldenring, armoredcore6, nightreign. The [[natives]] loading mechanism every ER crate assumes does not exist here.
2. fromsoftware-rs has NO darksouls2 crate. Members are shared, shared/stl, darksouls3, eldenring, nightreign, sekiro. 21 of the 57 er-mods-rs crates depend on eldenring + fromsoftware-shared and are hard-blocked on bindings that do not exist.
3. DS2 SOTFS carries 48 Arxan stubs (dearxan analysis, all 48 analyzed OK). Any MinHook detour must survive their integrity checks.
design: Tiering by coupling, not by feature appeal. Tier 0 = loader + substrate (nothing can be validated without it). Tier 1 = crates with zero game coupling, portable today and cargo test-able on Linux. Tier 2 = logic ports blocked on DS2 Ghidra work. Tier 3 = engine-generation mismatch (D3D11 vs D3D12, no Scaleform, different formats) -- rewrite, not port.

title: Runtime-validate ds2-crash-logging in DARK SOULS II
description:
ds2-mods-rs-fuv was force-closed on the PORT; this is the runtime half it could not do.

Once the dinput8 proxy loads and Arxan is neutered, confirm ds2_crash_logging.dll actually captures a fault inside DarkSoulsII.exe: crash log written to the Game/ directory, the faulting module and its RVA recorded, previous_unhandled_filter chained rather than swallowed, and the minidump tier that survives Proton's dbghelp identified.

Known unknowns going in:
- Whether the game (or Steam/Proton) installs its own unhandled-exception filter that this chains onto, and whether that one still runs.
- Which minidump tier Proton's dbghelp accepts. In ../er-mods-rs both rich and normal tiers failed with ERROR_NOACCESS (998) and only the no-exception-parameter tier worked; under a plain Wine prefix here the RICH tier succeeded (type=0x1160). Do not assume either result carries over.
- Whether Arxan's integrity checks object to a vectored handler at all (it patches no game code, so probably not -- but that is a guess until it runs).

Deliberately faulting a thread on purpose is the test. See crates/ds2-crash-logging/examples/load_and_crash.rs for the game-free version of it.

title: Port check-fresh-run-logs.py so the one-log-per-run rule is executable
description: ds2-game-base::log documents a standing rule -- no log may be appended to across process runs -- and provides begin_fresh_run/open_fresh_run_append as the only sanctioned openers. In ../er-mods-rs that rule is enforced by scripts/check-fresh-run-logs.py, which fails the build on any OpenOptions::append() outside that module. No such check exists here, so the rule currently holds only by convention. Port the script and wire it into scripts/check.sh.

title: Tier 1: ds2-crash-logging -- first real mod, no DS2 RE required
description:
er-crash-logging-core depends only on er-game-base. First-chance exceptions to a text file via a Win32 vectored exception handler. Near-generic -- the DS2-specific part is only the module name it symbolizes against.

This is the right FIRST REAL MOD: it proves the dinput8 loader, the Arxan neutering and the log path end to end while needing zero knowledge of DS2 structures. If it works, the substrate is real; if it does not, nothing built on top of it would have worked either.
acceptance_criteria: ds2_crash_logging.dll loads under Proton via the dinput8 proxy and writes a crash log for a deliberately faulted thread, with the faulting module and RVA recorded.
close_reason:
Code ported and merged as PR #4 (draft): crates/ds2-crash-logging-core + crates/ds2-crash-logging, building as ds2_crash_logging.dll. Gate passes (scripts/check.sh --host-tests) and the release cdylib builds.

Force-closed over the open edge to ds2-mods-rs-31p (Arxan) on purpose, and the dependency graph is NOT edited. That edge is real -- but it blocks the RUNTIME VALIDATION in this issue's acceptance criteria ("loads under Proton via the dinput8 proxy and writes a crash log for a deliberately faulted thread"), not the port. The DLL cannot be loaded into DS2 until the dinput8 proxy exists (ds2-mods-rs-loader work) and Arxan's integrity checks are neutered (ds2-mods-rs-31p), both owned elsewhere. Nothing in this crate has been run against the game.

What WAS validated, without the game: the load_and_crash example loads the DLL into a throwaway process under Wine and raises 0xc0000005. All five artifacts were written, the identity line opened the log, addresses resolved against the loader's module table (exception_address=0x6fffff32d967{kernelbase.dll+0xd967}), and the rich minidump tier succeeded. 12 host unit tests cover the classification, budget and module/RVA resolution logic.

Two corrections to this issue's own description:
1. "the DS2-specific part is only the module name it symbolizes against" -- not true of the port. Nothing is symbolized against a named module; the PEB InMemoryOrderModuleList supplies base/span/name per image at runtime, so there is no module name in the code at all and ds2-rva stays empty.
2. er-crash-logging-core is NOT near-generic. Its hang.rs (1,585 lines, half the crate) is built entirely on Elden Ring facts -- GAME_FRAME_COUNTER_RVA 0x3d8_567c on eldenring.exe 1.16.2, GAME_MODULE_NAME "eldenring.exe", and CS::LoadingScreenData field offsets -- and did not port. A DS2 hang watchdog needs DS2's per-frame counter found in the disassembly first; that is new work, not a port.

Follow-up work worth its own issue: re-run the acceptance criteria in-game once the loader and Arxan issues land, and (separately) a DS2 hang watchdog once a frame counter RVA exists in ds2-rva.

title: Tier 2: ds2-net-effects -- first mod needing real DS2 Ghidra work
description:
er-net-effects is the original feature of er-mods-rs: keyboard-selected SpEffects applied to the player, network sync default OFF. Depends on er-hotkey-config, eldenring, fromsoftware-shared, er-quickload-data, er-hook, er-game-base, hudhook, er-build-watermark-core.

DS2 has SpEffects too, so the FEATURE ports; the plumbing does not. Needs from Ghidra: the DS2 player-character structure, the apply-SpEffect function address, and the SpEffectParam id space. Everything above the hotkey layer is already portable via ds2-hotkey-config.

Natural first gameplay mod because it is a single function call against a single structure -- the smallest possible bet on the DS2 bindings work being right.

title: Tier 2: fromsoftware-rs darksouls2 bindings crate (model on darksouls3, not eldenring)
description:
21 of the 57 er-mods-rs crates depend on 'eldenring' + 'fromsoftware-shared'. fromsoftware-rs has no darksouls2 member (only shared, shared/stl, darksouls3, eldenring, nightreign, sekiro), so all 21 are hard-blocked.

Scale of the work, measured: crates/darksouls3 = 44,383 lines; crates/eldenring = 81,093; crates/shared = 8,434.

Model on darksouls3, NOT eldenring -- DS3 (2016) is one generation from DS2 (2014); ER is three. The DS3 crate's module layout is app_menu, cs, dlio, dlkr, dltx, dlui, dlut, fd4, param, rva, sprj, stl, util. Expect a DS2 crate to keep far less of that: DS2 predates the FD4 framework and most of the DL* subsystem naming, so the bindings must come from the Ghidra work by hand rather than from reflection metadata.
notes: This is the single largest item in the port and gates every gameplay mod. Do not start it before Tier 0 and Tier 1 land -- they need none of it.

title: Tier 1: ds2-hotkey-config + ds2-safe-input -- verbatim ports, zero game coupling
description:
These need no DS2 reverse engineering and are cargo test-able on Linux with no game attached:

er-hotkey-config (1708 lines: binding.rs 221, keys.rs 988, lib.rs 42, live.rs 150, reload.rs 307). Zero game deps. User-nameable hotkeys with reload-without-restart. Straight copy.

er-safe-input (233 lines). Models controller/menu intent (SafeButton: Confirm/Cancel/Start/Dpad*/Bumpers) rather than raw key injection; backends map intent to a mechanism. Zero game coupling. Straight copy. Relevant that DS2 imports DINPUT8.dll and XINPUT1_3.dll, so both backends have a target.

er-crash-logging-core (depends only on er-game-base). First-chance exceptions to a text file. Near-generic Win32 vectored exception handling -- the best FIRST REAL MOD because it proves the loader, the Arxan neutering and the log path while needing zero DS2 structure knowledge.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test passes on Linux for the ported host-side crates; ds2_crash_logging.dll loads under Proton and writes a crash log for a deliberately faulted thread.

title: Frida: port the gadget-host mechanism (NOT the ERSC scripts) when runtime tracing is actually needed
description:
Deferred deliberately, not rejected. ~18 Frida scripts exist in ../er-mods-rs/scripts/. Most do not port; the mechanism does.

WHAT DOES NOT PORT (~13 of 18): frida-ersc-session-trace, frida-lobby-watch-members, frida-lobby-read-keys, frida-session-lobby-fields, frida-steam-lobby-keys, frida-steam-matchmaking-trace, frida-steam-vtable-trace, frida-steam-filter-probe, frida-invader-filter-capture, frida-invasion-mechanism-trace, frida-hunt-drive-query. All Seamless Co-op / Steam lobby / matchmaking / invasion internals -- Tier 3, no DS2 analogue.

WHAT DOES PORT -- the attach mechanism. From frida-dump-module.py's own docstring: 'The game runs under Wine/Proton, so a Linux-side frida.attach() sees nothing -- there is no Linux process to attach to. frida-gadget.dll is loaded INTO the game as an me3 [[natives]] entry and listens on 127.0.0.1:27042; we connect to that as a REMOTE DEVICE.' 13 of the scripts use frida.get_device_manager() + attach('Gadget').

THE ADAPTATION: that recipe depends on me3 [[natives]], which DS2 does not have (all three me3 entry paths refused -- see docs/LOADING.md). But crates/ds2-loader's dinput8 proxy already loads into the process before the entry point and is proven in-game. Make it load frida-gadget.dll and the rest of the approach transfers unchanged.

Also worth taking: the selftest discipline in those scripts (a --selftest mode that proves the assembly logic with no game and no frida, so a live run is not spent discovering a bug in the script).

No system install needed: the scripts run under 'uv run --with frida python3 ...'.
notes: WHY DEFERRED: (1) M1 (does a MinHook detour survive Arxan) is unfinished, and a Frida gadget inside an Arxan process is the same class of question -- doing both at once puts two unknowns in one experiment. (2) No static RE has been done at all yet, and the binary is heavily symbolized: 5271 RTTI type descriptors, 587 DLRF-registered classes. Standing up runtime tracing before reading a fully-symbolized binary is scaffolding around the question rather than an answer to it. Port scripts/ghidra/ first.

title: Find DS2's per-frame counter, then decide on a hang watchdog
description:
er-crash-logging-core ships a second module, hang.rs (1,585 lines), that reports FREEZES -- which raise no exception and are invisible to the crash logger. It did NOT port with ds2-crash-logging, because all three of its detectors sit on Elden Ring facts:

- GAME_FRAME_COUNTER_RVA = 0x3d8_567c: the dword MainUpdate increments once per frame, on eldenring.exe 1.16.2. Written by INC dword ptr [0x143d8567c] at 0x140dea394.
- GAME_MODULE_NAME = "eldenring.exe": checked case-insensitively before that RVA is read at all.
- CS::LoadingScreenData field offsets, verified against live values on 1.16.2. FD4-era class; DS2 predates it.

Strip those and what remains is a thread-suspension harness with nothing to watch.

Step one is reverse engineering, not code: find the dword DS2's main loop increments once per frame in darksoulsii-deobf.bin, and put its RVA in ds2-rva. The er-mods-rs design is worth copying wholesale once that exists -- it refuses to arm until it has actually WATCHED the counter advance ARM_ADVANCES_REQUIRED times, so a game patch that moves the field disarms the watchdog and says so instead of reporting a permanent fake hang. It also never allocates while a thread is suspended, which would deadlock the process it is diagnosing.

The loading-screen oracle is a separate question and probably a rewrite: it needs whatever DS2's equivalent of a load-progress object is, if there is one.

Blocked on ds2-mods-rs-fuv's crate existing (it does) and on RE that has not started.

title: Decide Cargo.lock policy once the Tier 0 waves have landed
description:
Cargo.lock is currently UNTRACKED, and both wave-1 agents independently made that call for the same reason: every parallel branch that adds a crate rewrites the lock, so committing it puts them all in conflict on one file -- exactly what the glob `members = ["crates/*"]` in the root Cargo.toml exists to prevent.

That reasoning is right DURING a fan-out and wrong afterwards. This workspace ships cdylibs to players; a reproducible dependency set is the normal expectation for a binary artifact, and an untracked lock means two builds of the same commit can differ.

Decision to make once Tier 0 is merged and the parallel branches are done: commit Cargo.lock in a single dedicated commit on main, and from then on treat a lock conflict as an ordinary rebase, not a design flaw.
notes: Filed from the wave-1 agent reports (PR #1 and PR #2), both of which flagged it unprompted and left the lock untracked to match main.

title: Tier 3: DO NOT PORT -- engine-generation mismatches, catalogue the rewrites
description:
Crates whose ER implementation cannot be ported because the DS2 engine differs in kind, not degree:

D3D12 -> D3D11. DS2 SOTFS imports d3d11.dll and dxgi.dll (verified in its import table). er-d3d12-compositor (818 lines) and everything on it -- er-loading-bar, er-loading-portrait -- need a D3D11 compositor written from scratch. hudhook has a D3D11 backend, so the hudhook-based crates (er-build-watermark-core, er-invasion-path, er-net-effects overlay) have a path; the bespoke D3D12 compositor does not.

Scaleform. er-scaleform-hooks and er-gfx assume the ER menu system is Scaleform GFx. UNVERIFIED for DS2 -- check before assuming either way; DS2 shows no Scaleform import but it could be statically linked.

Boot/menu machinery. er-quickload, er-save-picker-core/-picker, er-quit-menu-core/-menu, er-title-flow, er-profile-summary-core all sit on ER's InGameStep / CSMenuMan / Scaleform / D3D12 stack. Rewrites.

Multiplayer. er-invasion-path (Havok-AI navmesh), er-invasion-warp (CSAutoInvadePoint), er-seamless-bugfixes (Seamless Co-op specific) have no DS2 analogue.

Formats. soulsformats, er-tpf, er-flver, erpx-rs target ER format versions. DS2 differs: params have a different layout and the regulation is enc_regulation.bnd.dcx (AES) rather than regulation.bin. Partial reuse at best.
